clues: This city in South America lies on a flat plain by the coast, just south of a long point of land. The warm sea by its port is a short ride away.
This hot place stays dry in a strange way. The sun and air pull so much water from the ground that the land stays semi-dry, though rain does fall each year.
This city was founded on July 26 in the year 1527 by Juan de Ampíes, a man from Spain. It is the second oldest city in its whole land.
From 1528 to 1546, a rich family from Germany ran this town. It was the first town held by that land in all of the New World.
Its well kept old town, built in the days of Spanish rule, is a World Heritage Site. Since 2005, that same site has been on a list of sites in danger.
